evidence: Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748), vol. 1, ch. 1, §2: Quantitās variābilis est quantitās indētermināta seu ūniversālis
terms.comment: The mathematicians’ term, defined by Euler; a constant is quantitās cōnstāns (§1). The adjective variābilis is post-classical (Apul.; Lewis & Short).
Our shortening of quantitās variābilis, for speech, as the modern languages shorten it. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for a variable.

sources: Lewis & Short: variabilis · Lewis & Short: quantitas
Leonhard Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (Lausanne, 1748), vol. 1, ch. 1, §§1–2.
